overview: This single-page file consists of a “List of Papers” indexing correspondence about plant-quarantine regulations in Japanese-ruled Formosa (Taiwan). The entries record notification that the regulations had been amended, the enclosure of revised Forms 7 and 8 for certifying plants examined for export, transmission of copies to relevant authorities, and a referenced communication from Taihoku concerning the regulations in force in Taiwan. The surviving OCR is substantially garbled in the final entry, particularly its date and routing information.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning plant-quarantine regulations in Formosa
subfiles.about: An administrative index records correspondence concerning amendments to Formosa’s plant-quarantine regulations and the distribution of revised export-examination certificates.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists December correspondence reporting that the Government of Formosa had amended its plant-quarantine regulations and enclosing new Forms 7 and 8 of the Certificate of Examination of Plants for Export. A subsequent entry states that copies of the regulations were transmitted to the appropriate authorities. A final, heavily garbled entry refers to Taihoku, Warner, and copies of plant-quarantine regulations in force in Taiwan.

interest: The page is useful as an administrative roadmap to correspondence that may no longer be present in the surviving bundle. It documents the practical regulation of plant exports from colonial Taiwan and shows quarantine information circulating between the Japanese Embassy and other authorities. Its reference to revised certificate forms offers evidence of the paperwork and enforcement mechanisms used to control plant pests and diseases, although the badly corrupted final entry requires consultation of the original image for reliable interpretation.
